input.rationale: Instrumented the append side - the gap-4 discriminator - and the draft-side run names the proposer state for the rejected history. For seed 35 the configuration change at index 4, term 2 was appended by node 2 at the same step as the first rejection (step 22) with pending_conf_index_before=2, applied_before=3, joint_before=false and validation_disabled=false. That tells two things. First, the guard's own clauses were satisfied in the ordinary way: alreadyPending was false because pendingConfIndex (2) did not exceed applied (3), and alreadyJoint was false because the appender's tracker was not joint. Second, and this is what keeps the claim unresolved rather than asserted, those operands conflict with the history the rejecting nodes hold: if node 2 had applied three entries of the same log whose index 2 is a joint-enter change, its tracker would be joint at that point, so either node 2's own entries differ from the log the others applied (a divergence the sweep's invariants did not flag because they compare committed (index, term) only at check points and only against the value first observed) or the harness produced a tracker state that its log does not imply - the restart path is a plausible source, since it rebuilds a node with the ConfState its tracker currently has while its log may already contain a joint change it has not applied. I record the operands as behaviour knowledge pending a receipt and note the next operand that would settle it: node 2's own entry types and terms for indices 1..4 at the moment of the append, which would show whether its log diverged or its tracker was rebuilt.

knowledge.statement: Draft-side observation of the append that produced the rejected history (sweep revision that records the appender's state): the joint-entering change at index 4, term 2 was appended by node 2 while pendingConfIndex was 2, applied was 3, the tracker was NOT joint and DisableConfChangeValidation was false, so both propose-time clauses were false in the ordinary way (pendingConfIndex did not exceed applied; the tracker was not joint). Every other append recorded in the same run shows the same shape - applied >= pendingConfIndex and joint_before=false - including cases where the appender had applied a dozen entries. That conflicts with the rejected nodes' history, whose index 2 is a joint-enter change: applying it in order would leave the applier joint, so the appender's tracked configuration and its log disagree at that point.
knowledge.conditions: Sweep revision with four real raft instances (node 4 registered directly and starting outside the configuration), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts rebuilt from persisted hard state and ConfState, default DisableConfChangeValidation; operands recorded at each append (seed, step, node, entry index and term, pendingConfIndex, applied, tracker jointness, validation flag). Draft-side only: no controller receipt yet.

knowledge.statement: campaign() enumerates only r.trk.Voters.IDs() and sends the self-vote as a self-addressed MsgVoteResp/MsgPreVoteResp through r.send, which routes vote responses into msgsAfterAppend so the self-vote is counted only after the term/vote is durable; poll() records the first vote seen per ID via ProgressTracker.RecordVote and TallyVotes returns Voters.VoteResult over the joint config, so a joint quorum requires a majority in both halves and learners or IDs outside the config contribute no votes.
knowledge.conditions: State machine in StateCandidate/StatePreCandidate after campaign() or campaignPreElection(); CheckQuorum/PreVote per Config.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe read confirmation is count-based: readOnly.addRequest appends the request with the commit index observed at admission, heartbeatCtx encodes confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) as an 8-byte little-endian position, recvAck stores per-voter maxima of echoed positions (including the leader's own ack taken immediately in sendMsgReadIndexResponse), and maybeAdvance releases a prefix of unconfirmedReads only when quorum.CommittedIndex over those per-voter positions covers it. The leader postpones MsgReadIndex into pendingReadIndexMessages while it has not committed an entry in its current term, and reset() (any term change) discards readOnly together with all unconfirmed reads and acks.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlyOption=ReadOnlySafe on a leader; the release happens in stepLeader's MsgHeartbeatResp path after readOnly.recvAck.

knowledge.statement: hup() returns without campaigning when the node is unpromotable (not in the progress map, learner, or holding an unstable/in-progress snapshot) or when hasUnappliedConfChanges() finds an EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2 in the index range (applied, committed]; the same guard therefore also applies to the leadership-transfer path, which reaches campaign() only through MsgTimeoutNow -> hup(campaignTransfer).
knowledge.conditions: Any MsgHup, whether from tickElection or from MsgTimeoutNow on a follower, at the term and log state of the node.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun a8e8732ff16b4c37b22e79408d1f066a, indices 10-15): a 3-node leader that has committed an entry in its term and replicated a committed ConfChangeV2 learner addition to follower 2 (leader StateLeader term 1 committed 2; r2 StateFollower applied 0 committed 2 hasUnappliedConfChanges true; leader's Match for r2 == lastIndex 2) accepts its own TransferLeader request to r2 by setting leadTransferee 2 while r2 remains StateFollower at term 1, rejects a proposal with ErrProposalDropped during the pending window, clears leadTransferee to 0 after the leader's electionTimeout ticks while the leader stays leader at term 1 and proposals are accepted again, and completes the retried transfer once the transferee's applied index reaches its committed index (transferee StateLeader term 2, former leader StateFollower term 2). The transfer duty is therefore delayed and bounded by the transferee's application lag, not lost.

knowledge.statement: In this snapshot the configuration a restarted raft instance adopts comes from Storage.InitialState's ConfState: newRaft takes cs from c.Storage.InitialState() and feeds it to confchange.Restore, and MemoryStorage.InitialState returns ms.snapshot.GetMetadata().GetConfState() (passed through pb.EnsureConfState). MemoryStorage only changes that ConfState when the caller supplies one - ApplySnapshot installs the snapshot it is given (with the snapshot-only-ConfState bootstrap case allowed when the stored snapshot index is 0) and CreateSnapshot copies the caller's cs parameter into the metadata - while Append and Compact never touch the metadata, so a node restarted from a MemoryStorage that only ever had entries appended adopts the configuration that was present when the snapshot metadata was written.
knowledge.conditions: MemoryStorage used as Storage for newRaft/RestartNode or for a harness that persists Ready.Entries and later restarts a node; no external ConfState is supplied between the initial configuration and the restart.

knowledge.statement: In the sweep as written (persist/apply every step for every node through nextEnts, which advances the applied index to the committed index), no check point ever observes a committed-but-unapplied configuration change at any node: the antecedent counter added to the liveness witness reports unapplied_conf_change_states=0 together with stalled_states=0 over 60 seeds x 60 steps. Consequently the witness's zero count is uninformative about the campaign guard: it counts the conjunction 'unapplied change present and nothing promotable', and its first conjunct never held. The counts only become evidence about the guard once the event set can leave application behind, for example by applying only a subset of nodes in a step or skipping the apply step for a chosen node.
knowledge.conditions: Draft-side run of draft/assurance_generated_test.go revision with the antecedent counter, same event mix as the previous revision (four nodes, node 4 starting outside the configuration, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, restart events); no controller receipt for this counter yet.

knowledge.assertion: a restarted instance adopts the configuration from Storage.InitialState's ConfState, so application lag is what leaves a committed change unapplied

knowledge.statement: Propose-time: stepLeader's MsgProp path computes alreadyPending = pendingConfIndex > raftLog.applied and, unless Config.DisableConfChangeValidation is set, rewrites a proposed conf change to a normal entry for that condition and for the alreadyJoint/wantsLeaveJoint mismatches, evaluated against the leader's own tracker. Apply-side: a joint-entering change applied at a node whose tracker is joint is still rejected with 'config is already joint' - the deterministic case shows the precondition (CheckRun eb27767ba74043ada1911d66fc9c4188 index 16), and the sweep with application lag and configuration events aimed at serving members now records three such rejections inside one run (invalid_change_applies=3 with reasons all 'config is already joint' against 245 configuration changes), with no invariant violation. The two guards are therefore not a complete exclusion of the shape: the propose-time check bounds what the leader may append given its own applied configuration, but a node can still be handed a joint-entering change while its own configuration is joint when the lagging configuration belongs to that node rather than to the leader.
knowledge.conditions: Leader-side check as before. Apply-side observation: sweep revision with application lag (one node's apply skipped about one time in six), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, restarts, four real state machines in one process.

knowledge.assertion: the campaign admission guard shares the same applied/committed gap that lets a configuration change be committed but unapplied at a node

history.statement: Two target-side guards together keep a joint-entering configuration change from being appended behind an unapplied configuration change: stepLeader's MsgProp path sets alreadyPending = pendingConfIndex > raftLog.applied and, unless Config.DisableConfChangeValidation is set, replaces a proposed conf change with a normal entry in that case (and likewise for alreadyJoint && !wantsLeaveJoint and !alreadyJoint && wantsLeaveJoint), while becomeLeader conservatively initializes pendingConfIndex to the last log index and appliedTo raises it when a change is applied. At the apply side the same ordering is satisfied by the target itself: applying a joint change with AutoLeave set makes appliedTo propose the zero-change leave-joint entry, which the Changer requires to be applied before another joint-entering change can be accepted (observed: a second joint-entering change applied while joint is rejected with 'config is already joint', and the same change is accepted after the leave-joint change, CheckRun eb27767ba74043ada1911d66fc9c4188 index 16). The residual case is Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, documented as requiring the user to serialize and verify configuration changes, with an invalid change reaching the log panicking by design.
history.conditions: Leader-side: any MsgProp carrying EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2 at the leader's current applied index and configuration. Apply-side: applyConfChange on a node whose tracker is joint when a joint-entering change is applied. Config.DisableConfChangeValidation defaults to false.

knowledge.assertion: the same applied/committed gap drives the campaign admission guard through a paginated scan of the unapplied commit range

history.correction: The previous revision concluded that for the default configuration the ordering requirement is enforced at propose time and satisfied at apply time by auto-leave, with the residual case limited to Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, and that the earlier harness panic was therefore a harness modelling error rather than a shape reachable through permitted histories. The sweep now reaches the shape with default validation: three apply-side rejections with reason 'config is already joint' in one run while the four invariants held, so the premise that the guards exclude the shape must be narrowed to 'the guards bound what the leader appends given its own applied configuration; they do not exclude a joint-entering change reaching a node whose own configuration is joint'. The remaining unresolved part is the exact entry order at the rejecting node, which the sweep does not record and which a deterministic prefix must preserve.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad indices 17-19, summary at 20): three nodes consuming their own committed logs in order (applied_before=3 and applying_before=3 for nodes 3 and 1, applied_before=0 for a node rebuilt from persisted state, reapplied_entry=false everywhere) reject a committed entry at index 4, term 2, a single-change joint-entering ConfChangeV2, with the Changer's message 'config is already joint', while their entry sequences are identical: '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' - normal, ConfChangeV2, normal, ConfChangeV2 - so the log contains a second joint-entering configuration change with no leave-joint entry between the two, and the only intervening entry is a normal one, which is what the target's own propose-time rewrite substitutes for a configuration change it refuses to append. The same run reports violations=0 for at-least-one-leader-per-term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity and applied<=committed, and 245 configuration change proposals produced exactly these three rejections.
knowledge.conditions: Four real raft instances in one process (nodes 1..4, node 4 starting outside the configuration), configuration changes proposed as single-change ConfChangeV2 on the leader with a target drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, half of them with Transition=JointImplicit, application lag that skips one node's apply step about one time in six, node restarts from persisted hard state and applied ConfState, DisableConfChangeValidation left at its default false.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun 93a96c7d08e749dea498a75f9e66f17c index 16): a leader whose log already holds a committed joint-entering ConfChangeV2 it has not applied (pending_conf_index=0, applied=0, committed=2, joint_now=false) accepts a second joint-entering proposal through the real MsgProp path and appends it as EntryConfChangeV2 at index 3 - the guard's alreadyPending and alreadyJoint clauses are both false in that state, so the proposal is not rewritten to a normal entry. The same receipt's sweep indices (18-20) show the consequence at three other nodes: the log '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' is applied in order and the second configuration change is rejected with 'config is already joint'.
knowledge.conditions: Single voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) that has become candidate and leader; the committed joint change is appended and committed by the case while the node's applied index stays at 0, and pendingConfIndex is set to the applied index, which is the staleness a leadership change can leave behind; DisableConfChangeValidation at its default false.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun aa600f3fb29146a99e15abbec79139fd indices 18-20): the committed history the three rejecting nodes consumed in order is index 2 = ConfChangeV2 transition JointImplicit removing node 4 (change type 1, node 4) and index 4 = ConfChangeV2 transition JointImplicit adding node 4 (change type 0, node 4), with a normal entry at index 3 between them and no leave-joint entry anywhere in the range [firstIndex, committed]. So the log enters a joint configuration through a change that removes a node which is not a member of the voter set - a change that alters nothing about who votes - and then enters a second joint configuration from within the first, which is the entry each node's Changer rejects with 'config is already joint'.
knowledge.conditions: Sweep revision with four real raft instances, configuration targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts, default DisableConfChangeValidation; the rejecting nodes are 3, 1 and 4 at seed 35.

knowledge.statement: appliedTo only proposes the zero-change leave-joint entry when the node applying the committed entries is the leader: the branch is `r.trk.Config.AutoLeave && newApplied >= r.pendingConfIndex && r.state == StateLeader`, and it then steps a proposal built by confChangeToMsg(nil), whose comment notes it can only be dropped by an in-progress leadership transfer. Consequently a joint configuration entered by a change that some node other than the current leader applies stays joint until a leader applies that entry (or a later one) and proposes the leave; if the leader that proposed the joint change loses leadership before applying it, no leave is proposed by anyone until a later leader applies the change, and until then every node that has applied it holds a joint configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Leader-side: appliedTo called with newApplied >= pendingConfIndex while the node is StateLeader and the current configuration has AutoLeave set (which JointImplicit and Auto transitions set). Follower-side: the same apply on a non-leader performs no proposal.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun d75f65e79d2d46c0ae313cb0c5532795 index 17): applying a ConfChangeV2 with Transition=JointImplicit whose single change removes node 4 - a node that is not in the voter set - leaves the node in a joint configuration (joint=true, auto_leave=true) with voters unchanged at [1,2,3] and outgoing_size equal to incoming_size (3). A configuration change that alters no membership therefore still enters joint consensus and still requires a leave-joint entry to exit it, and per the auto-leave guard that entry is only ever proposed by a node that is leader when it applies the change.
knowledge.conditions: One voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) handed the change through applyConfChange directly; node 4 absent from the configuration by construction.

Consequently the witness's zero count is uninformative about the campaign guard: it counts the conjunction 'unapplied change present and nothing promotable', and its first conjunct never held. The counts only become evidence about the guard once the event set can leave application behind, for example by applying only a subset of nodes in a step or skipping the apply step for a chosen node.
knowledge.conditions: Draft-side run of draft/assurance_generated_test.go revision with the antecedent counter, same event mix as the previous revision (four nodes, node 4 starting outside the configuration, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, restart events); no controller receipt for this counter yet.

knowledge.assertion: a restarted instance adopts the configuration from Storage.InitialState's ConfState, so application lag is what leaves a committed change unapplied

knowledge.statement: Propose-time: stepLeader's MsgProp path computes alreadyPending = pendingConfIndex > raftLog.applied and, unless Config.DisableConfChangeValidation is set, rewrites a proposed conf change to a normal entry for that condition and for the alreadyJoint/wantsLeaveJoint mismatches, evaluated against the leader's own tracker. Apply-side: a joint-entering change applied at a node whose tracker is joint is still rejected with 'config is already joint' - the deterministic case shows the precondition (CheckRun eb27767ba74043ada1911d66fc9c4188 index 16), and the sweep with application lag and configuration events aimed at serving members now records three such rejections inside one run (invalid_change_applies=3 with reasons all 'config is already joint' against 245 configuration changes), with no invariant violation. The two guards are therefore not a complete exclusion of the shape: the propose-time check bounds what the leader may append given its own applied configuration, but a node can still be handed a joint-entering change while its own configuration is joint when the lagging configuration belongs to that node rather than to the leader.
knowledge.conditions: Leader-side check as before. Apply-side observation: sweep revision with application lag (one node's apply skipped about one time in six), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, restarts, four real state machines in one process.

knowledge.assertion: the campaign admission guard shares the same applied/committed gap that lets a configuration change be committed but unapplied at a node

history.statement: Two target-side guards together keep a joint-entering configuration change from being appended behind an unapplied configuration change: stepLeader's MsgProp path sets alreadyPending = pendingConfIndex > raftLog.applied and, unless Config.DisableConfChangeValidation is set, replaces a proposed conf change with a normal entry in that case (and likewise for alreadyJoint && !wantsLeaveJoint and !alreadyJoint && wantsLeaveJoint), while becomeLeader conservatively initializes pendingConfIndex to the last log index and appliedTo raises it when a change is applied. At the apply side the same ordering is satisfied by the target itself: applying a joint change with AutoLeave set makes appliedTo propose the zero-change leave-joint entry, which the Changer requires to be applied before another joint-entering change can be accepted (observed: a second joint-entering change applied while joint is rejected with 'config is already joint', and the same change is accepted after the leave-joint change, CheckRun eb27767ba74043ada1911d66fc9c4188 index 16). The residual case is Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, documented as requiring the user to serialize and verify configuration changes, with an invalid change reaching the log panicking by design.
history.conditions: Leader-side: any MsgProp carrying EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2 at the leader's current applied index and configuration. Apply-side: applyConfChange on a node whose tracker is joint when a joint-entering change is applied. Config.DisableConfChangeValidation defaults to false.

knowledge.assertion: the same applied/committed gap drives the campaign admission guard through a paginated scan of the unapplied commit range

history.correction: The previous revision concluded that for the default configuration the ordering requirement is enforced at propose time and satisfied at apply time by auto-leave, with the residual case limited to Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, and that the earlier harness panic was therefore a harness modelling error rather than a shape reachable through permitted histories. The sweep now reaches the shape with default validation: three apply-side rejections with reason 'config is already joint' in one run while the four invariants held, so the premise that the guards exclude the shape must be narrowed to 'the guards bound what the leader appends given its own applied configuration; they do not exclude a joint-entering change reaching a node whose own configuration is joint'. The remaining unresolved part is the exact entry order at the rejecting node, which the sweep does not record and which a deterministic prefix must preserve.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad indices 17-19, summary at 20): three nodes consuming their own committed logs in order (applied_before=3 and applying_before=3 for nodes 3 and 1, applied_before=0 for a node rebuilt from persisted state, reapplied_entry=false everywhere) reject a committed entry at index 4, term 2, a single-change joint-entering ConfChangeV2, with the Changer's message 'config is already joint', while their entry sequences are identical: '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' - normal, ConfChangeV2, normal, ConfChangeV2 - so the log contains a second joint-entering configuration change with no leave-joint entry between the two, and the only intervening entry is a normal one, which is what the target's own propose-time rewrite substitutes for a configuration change it refuses to append. The same run reports violations=0 for at-least-one-leader-per-term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity and applied<=committed, and 245 configuration change proposals produced exactly these three rejections.
knowledge.conditions: Four real raft instances in one process (nodes 1..4, node 4 starting outside the configuration), configuration changes proposed as single-change ConfChangeV2 on the leader with a target drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, half of them with Transition=JointImplicit, application lag that skips one node's apply step about one time in six, node restarts from persisted hard state and applied ConfState, DisableConfChangeValidation left at its default false.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun 93a96c7d08e749dea498a75f9e66f17c index 16): a leader whose log already holds a committed joint-entering ConfChangeV2 it has not applied (pending_conf_index=0, applied=0, committed=2, joint_now=false) accepts a second joint-entering proposal through the real MsgProp path and appends it as EntryConfChangeV2 at index 3 - the guard's alreadyPending and alreadyJoint clauses are both false in that state, so the proposal is not rewritten to a normal entry. The same receipt's sweep indices (18-20) show the consequence at three other nodes: the log '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' is applied in order and the second configuration change is rejected with 'config is already joint'.
knowledge.conditions: Single voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) that has become candidate and leader; the committed joint change is appended and committed by the case while the node's applied index stays at 0, and pendingConfIndex is set to the applied index, which is the staleness a leadership change can leave behind; DisableConfChangeValidation at its default false.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun aa600f3fb29146a99e15abbec79139fd indices 18-20): the committed history the three rejecting nodes consumed in order is index 2 = ConfChangeV2 transition JointImplicit removing node 4 (change type 1, node 4) and index 4 = ConfChangeV2 transition JointImplicit adding node 4 (change type 0, node 4), with a normal entry at index 3 between them and no leave-joint entry anywhere in the range [firstIndex, committed]. So the log enters a joint configuration through a change that removes a node which is not a member of the voter set - a change that alters nothing about who votes - and then enters a second joint configuration from within the first, which is the entry each node's Changer rejects with 'config is already joint'.
knowledge.conditions: Sweep revision with four real raft instances, configuration targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts, default DisableConfChangeValidation; the rejecting nodes are 3, 1 and 4 at seed 35.

knowledge.statement: appliedTo only proposes the zero-change leave-joint entry when the node applying the committed entries is the leader: the branch is `r.trk.Config.AutoLeave && newApplied >= r.pendingConfIndex && r.state == StateLeader`, and it then steps a proposal built by confChangeToMsg(nil), whose comment notes it can only be dropped by an in-progress leadership transfer. Consequently a joint configuration entered by a change that some node other than the current leader applies stays joint until a leader applies that entry (or a later one) and proposes the leave; if the leader that proposed the joint change loses leadership before applying it, no leave is proposed by anyone until a later leader applies the change, and until then every node that has applied it holds a joint configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Leader-side: appliedTo called with newApplied >= pendingConfIndex while the node is StateLeader and the current configuration has AutoLeave set (which JointImplicit and Auto transitions set). Follower-side: the same apply on a non-leader performs no proposal.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun d75f65e79d2d46c0ae313cb0c5532795 index 17): applying a ConfChangeV2 with Transition=JointImplicit whose single change removes node 4 - a node that is not in the voter set - leaves the node in a joint configuration (joint=true, auto_leave=true) with voters unchanged at [1,2,3] and outgoing_size equal to incoming_size (3). A configuration change that alters no membership therefore still enters joint consensus and still requires a leave-joint entry to exit it, and per the auto-leave guard that entry is only ever proposed by a node that is leader when it applies the change.
knowledge.conditions: One voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) handed the change through applyConfChange directly; node 4 absent from the configuration by construction.

knowledge.statement: Draft-side observation of the append that produced the rejected history (sweep revision that records the appender's state): the joint-entering change at index 4, term 2 was appended by node 2 while pendingConfIndex was 2, applied was 3, the tracker was NOT joint and DisableConfChangeValidation was false, so both propose-time clauses were false in the ordinary way (pendingConfIndex did not exceed applied; the tracker was not joint). Every other append recorded in the same run shows the same shape - applied >= pendingConfIndex and joint_before=false - including cases where the appender had applied a dozen entries. That conflicts with the rejected nodes' history, whose index 2 is a joint-enter change: applying it in order would leave the applier joint, so the appender's tracked configuration and its log disagree at that point.
knowledge.conditions: Sweep revision with four real raft instances (node 4 registered directly and starting outside the configuration), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts rebuilt from persisted hard state and ConfState, default DisableConfChangeValidation; operands recorded at each append (seed, step, node, entry index and term, pendingConfIndex, applied, tracker jointness, validation flag). Draft-side only: no controller receipt yet.
